gates.claim: the dilogarithm half, now PROVED in Lean for the corpus's cLiTwoExt (im_cLiTwoExt_exp): Im Li_2(e^{i theta}) = Cl_2(theta) on (0, 2pi). Proved by same-derivative -- both sides differentiate to -log(2 sin(theta/2)) -- plus the basepoint theta = pi, where cLiTwoExt(-1) = -pi^2/12 is REAL and Cl_2(pi) = 0

THE LAW OF SINES for an ideal tetrahedron: |z| = sin(th2)/sin(th3), with the three angles summing to pi. The ideal-tetrahedron analogue of the Euclidean law of sines -- the MODULUS of the shape is a ratio of sines of opposite angles, just as a side length is in a triangle. It ties the ANGLE picture to the SHAPE-PARAMETER picture, and it holds at the 5_2 shape y_1 like everywhere else

THE REDUCTION WORKS. Along every ray of constant arg z, the difference (Lambda-side minus dilogarithm-side) is CONSTANT in r -- and equal to 0. That constancy is exactly what the law of sines buys, and it is why Kummer for general z needs only a ONE-variable argument with r = 1 as basepoint, not the two-variable differential argument it appears to need

SCOPE, UPDATED. When written this gate said the radial argument was not yet assembled and general-z Kummer was unproved. It is now PROVED -- QOU/Knot/KummerRadial.lean, `kummer`, sorry-free -- by exactly the reduction G3 anticipated. What remains untouched is Vol(5_2): Kummer is the ANALYTIC factor of Vol = D, and the GEOMETRIC factor (a triangulation's Lambda-sum IS the volume) is qou-m015/qou-krvm territory. The 5_2 volume conjecture is Ohtsuki's published theorem, not formalised anywhere here

verdict.proved: Kummer on |z| = 1 (both halves); the ideal-tetrahedron law of sines |z| = sin(th2)/sin(th3) for all Im z > 0.
verdict.also_proved: Kummer for general z -- QOU/Knot/KummerRadial.lean, `kummer`. The radial argument G3 anticipated is now assembled.
verdict.not_proved: Vol(5_2) -- the GEOMETRIC factor of Vol = D is untouched.
